messages:
maria-support: Hey team — customer is hitting persistent 429s during their nightly embeddings job (bulk ~100k docs). They run batches of 512 with concurrency 32 and report sporadic 'dimension mismatch' 400s for a handful of items. Need triage and quick mitigation, they're blocked for tomorrow's run.

alex-mlops: Can you paste the request + response headers and which model exactly? Also any client-side retry logic?

maria-support: Model: text-emb-redwood-1536 (customer said). Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings. Sample curl they used:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model": "text-emb-redwood-1536", "input": ["... 512 strings ..."]}'
```

Error fragment they pasted:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1729457200
```

And one of the 400s: `400 Bad Request — embedding vector length 384 != expected 1536` (appeared for ~0.02% of items).

jia-oncall: Looks like two things colliding: burst concurrency making them hit the burst-cap, and some payload items are old/precomputed 384-d vectors sneaking into the job (hence the dim mismatch). The Retry-After of 2s + X-RateLimit-Remaining 0 suggests they exhausted burst tokens. What does their client do on 429?

maria-support: They said they have a naive retry loop: on 429 they immediately retry up to 5x with no jitter. Also they spawn 32 workers each sending batches concurrently.

alex-mlops: That retry pattern will amplify the spike (thundering herd). Immediate mitigation for customer: 1) stop current run; 2) reduce concurrency to 4-8 workers; 3) reduce batch size to 256 (or 128 if memory permits); 4) implement exponential backoff with full jitter (e.g., base=0.5s, cap=60s, randomization). Also verify they are not sending precomputed vectors.

ops-bot: :warning: RATECAP alert — project=acct-12345 env=prod threshold=burst-limit reached at 2025-11-05T02:04:03Z (payload: bursts=18, sustained=3m)

support-engineer: For the dimension mismatch: ask them to run a quick validator before sending a batch. Example snippet to detect bad items:

```python
def validate_inputs(inputs, expected_dim=1536):
    bad = []
    for i, item in enumerate(inputs):
        if isinstance(item, list):
            if len(item) != expected_dim:
                bad.append((i, len(item)))
    return bad
```

If they precompute embeddings, they should POST to our vector upload endpoint instead of /v1/embeddings, or ensure the model matches.

maria-support: I'll send that validator. Also sharing a small repro they can run to see the 429 locally:

```bash
# parallel-fire is a small helper that fires N concurrent curl requests
parallel-fire --concurrency 32 --requests 100 \n  "curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{\"model\":\"text-emb-redwood-1536\",\"input\":[\"x\"]}'"
```

This will usually trigger burst caps in <2 minutes.

infra-eng: I'm creating a temporary infra ticket to review burst token allocation for acct-12345 and to see if we can grant a short-lived bump. Also will check autoscaler behavior (did it spin up instances or did ratecap block before scaling?).

alex-mlops: Thanks. Two longer-term recommendations: (a) server-side async / queueing option for very large jobs (we have a private job API in beta) and (b) add a client library helper that does chunking+backoff automatically. For now, infra ticket will help short term.

ops-bot: TICKET INF-4521 created by infra-eng: 'acct-12345 burst bump request + autoscale check'

maria-support: I'll coordinate with the customer to reschedule their run for tomorrow 03:00 UTC with reduced concurrency and our validator in place. Also asking them to attach logs showing the 400 dim errors so we can confirm if those are precomputed vectors. :thumbsup:

support-engineer: Small follow-ups to include in the support DM: - sample validator (above) - recommended retry pseudocode: exponential backoff + jitter - recommended concurrency/batch windows (4–8 workers, batches 128–256) - ask them to send full request/response headers (don't redact X-RateLimit-* fields)

maria-support: OK will send DM now and update thread after the scheduled run. If infra can confirm burst bump before 03:00 UTC that would be ideal.

jia-oncall: If we still see 429s after client mitigations, we'll temporarily throttle them server-side with a smooth rate limiter (avoid hard 0 remaining) and route retries to a backoff queue. Keeping me in the loop.

maria-support: Thanks all — assigning follow-up: @alex-mlops (infra ticket), @infra-eng (bump + scale check), @support-engineer (validator + DM), @jia-oncall (oncall watch window).

alex-mlops: I'll post INF-4521 updates here when I have them.

ops-bot: NOTE: autoscaler logs snapshot attached to INF-4521 (link: https://internal.redwood/infra/tickets/INF-4521/logs)

maria-support: closing loop for now, will reopen if the run still fails. Good triage everyone.
